original_title: Visible-Light-Induced Dearomative Heteroarylation of Anthracene Derivatives with Heteroarylnitriles via Combined Energy Transfer and Electron Transfer
title: Breaking anthracene's aromaticity with light instead of a reagent
blurb: Visible light drives energy transfer and electron transfer together, generating radical anion intermediates that couple to graft heteroaryl groups, mainly pyridine-type rings, onto anthracenes and dearomatize them in the process. The point of those pyridine rings is tuning fluorescence and antimicrobial activity, and the method reportedly holds across a range of polycyclic substrates.

original_title: Silver-Catalyzed Cascade Reactions for the Synthesis of Indopyran Pseudo-Natural Products as Potent Anti-tumor Agents
title: Indole-pyran hybrids built by silver catalysis, one of them actually kills cancer cells
blurb: A silver-catalyzed cascade stitches together pyran-fused indoles in one pot, 41 examples across three scaffolds and yields up to 93%. One compound, 3t, is the real result: single-digit micromolar IC50s against three tumor lines, G2/M arrest, apoptosis, and suppressed migration. Still cell-culture data, nobody's dosed an animal yet.

original_title: Covalent Dimerization of an Aza-5–7–7 Saddle Unlocks Fullerene Recognition toward Both C60 and C70 with Preference for C70
title: A saddle-shaped host that only binds fullerenes once you glue two of them together
blurb: The monomeric saddle binds no fullerenes on its own, but covalently dimerizing it into an S-shaped pair of concave cavities switches on binding to both C60 and C70, with a preference for C70, confirmed by X-ray and NMR/UV-vis titration. The payoff here is the dimerization step itself, not just a bigger pocket.

original_title: Nickel-Catalyzed C(sp3)–H Arylation for the trans -Selective Synthesis of Sterically Congested Cyclopropanes and Other Cycloalkanes
title: Nickel pulls off a trans-selective C–H arylation nobody's managed on gem-dimethyl cyclopropanes
blurb: Cheap, abundant nickel catalysis arylates the C(sp3)-H bonds of gem-dimethyl cyclopropanes with an uncommon trans selectivity that the usual 4d/5d-metal C–H activation chemistry hasn't pulled off. The authors themselves call it a preliminary strategy, so treat this as proof of concept rather than a finished method.

original_title: CuBr-Catalyzed Enantioselective Synthesis of Decahydroquinoxaline-Based Bis(propargylamines): Application to the Synthesis of an Axially Chiral Allene
title: A one-pot route to chiral bis(propargylamines) that ends in an axially chiral allene
blurb: CuBr runs a three-component coupling of terminal alkynes, aromatic aldehydes, and a C2-symmetric chiral diamine into decahydroquinoxaline-based bis(propargylamines), 58-93% yield and diastereomeric ratios up to 99:1. Feed one into ZnI2 and it converts cleanly into an axially chiral allene at 90% ee, which is the part that justifies building the whole three-component system.

original_title: Elucidating the Synergistic Role of K-Co-Cu Ternary Interfaces in Selective CO2 Hydrogenation to Ethylene: A Combined DFT and Microkinetic Modeling Study
title: DFT says it's the Co/Cu interface, not just the metals, steering CO2 toward ethylene
blurb: A DFT plus microkinetic modeling study on K2O-promoted Co2C surfaces finds that both the Co/Cu atomic ratio and how the two metals sit at the interface decide whether CO2 hydrogenation favors ethylene. Purely computational, so it's a design hypothesis for catalyst builders until someone actually makes the predicted interface and tests it.

original_title: Electrochemical One-Pot Diverse C(sp3)–X Bond (Including C–H, C–C, C–N, and C–O) Transformations and C(sp2)–H Acyloxylation of Alkylarenes
title: Ammonia is the quiet fix behind this electrochemical C–H/C–X cleanup
blurb: An electrochemical one-pot setup cleaves a grab bag of C(sp3)-X bonds and acyloxylates C(sp2)-H on alkylarenes without a transition metal or external oxidant. The actual find is that NH3 sharply boosts electrolyte conductivity, and the acyloxylation runs through an acetoxy radical rather than the usual nucleophilic AcO- pathway, which conveniently keeps the radical from decarboxylating.

original_title: Base and Nucleophilic Catalysis Enables Formal [3+2] Cycloaddition of Alkynyl Diazoketones and Aminomalonates: Access to γ,γ‐Disubstituted 3‐Pyrrolin‐2‐ones
title: Diazoketones and aminomalonates click into pyrrolinones via base and nucleophilic catalysis
blurb: A formal [3+2] cycloaddition between alkynyl diazoketones and aminomalonates builds γ,γ-disubstituted 3-pyrrolin-2-ones under mild conditions with broad substrate scope. It scales to gram quantities and the products take further downstream chemistry, so this reads like a usable heterocycle route rather than a one-off demonstration.

original_title: Dose dependent immune and antioxidant in responses to low dose radiation
title: Immune and antioxidant markers move with the dose, even at low-level radiation
blurb: Tracks how immune activity and antioxidant markers shift as radiation dose rises, with the dose-dependence holding even down at the low end.

original_title: The Convergent Synthetic Efforts toward Knightol and a Simplified Analog
title: A convergent path to knightol, the antibiofilm diterpene from the sea
blurb: Efforts toward total synthesis of (−)-knightol, a cembranoid natural product reported to fight Staph aureus biofilms, plus a simplified aryl analog built alongside it. The route splits into western and eastern fragments, the eastern one scalable to grams, joined by cross-electrophile coupling before the macrocycle closes and gets epoxidized and diversified.

original_title: Mechanistic Study of CO2 Reduction in a Metal Nanoparticle/Ligand-Based Nanoconfined Pocket
title: DFT checks how much a nanopocket actually buys you in CO2 reduction
blurb: A DFT comparison of CO2 reduction against the competing hydrogen evolution reaction on bare Ag, doubly confined Ag, and a ligand-based nanopocket, testing how much interfacial confinement helps selectivity by stabilizing the rate-determining intermediates. Computational only, so it's a lead for someone to go build and test.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Visible-Light-Promoted Radical Spirocyclization of 1,7-Enynes and α-Bromocarbonyl Compounds to Access Spirooxindole Derivatives
title: Visible light turns enynes into spirooxindoles in one step
blurb: A radical cascade pairs 1,7-enynes with α-bromocarbonyl compounds under visible light to build spirooxindole scaffolds in one pot with high diastereoselectivity, backed by a scale-up run. Control experiments trace the mechanism to a radical pathway with a 1,5-hydrogen shift along the way.

original_title: Domino effect enables dynamic electronic structure evolution for stable and efficient water purification
title: A catalyst that rewires itself mid-reaction to avoid the usual activity-stability trade-off
blurb: Single-atom catalysts for breaking down persistent organic pollutants usually trade activity for stability because the design is static. This MgCo dual-single-atom catalyst instead runs a domino process, the Mg site photoreducing O2 to H2O2 under light, letting the electronic structure shift through the reaction rather than sit fixed, aimed at stable water purification without the usual compromise.

original_title: Resolving Coordination-Dependent Bonding Selectivity at Gold–Sulfur Interfaces
title: What actually decides whether a thiol on gold stays protonated
blurb: Single-molecule STM break-junction measurements show that whether a thiol binds gold as intact Au–SH or deprotonates to Au–thiolate comes down to the local coordination environment of the Au atoms, not something fixed about the thiol. Checked in both solution and self-assembled monolayers.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Dual-State Fluorescence with Efficiency Close to Unity from D-π-A-Type Triarylborane-Based Naphthalenes
title: Triarylborane naphthalenes that fluoresce just as well solid or dissolved
blurb: Two new D-π-A naphthalenes, BNPh-Nap and BNOPh-Nap, pair an electron-poor boryl group with an electron-rich diarylamino one and post dual-state emission efficiency close to unity, bright in dilute solution and in the solid state alike, despite a core flat enough you'd expect the usual aggregation quenching.

original_title: Impact of Oral Cladribine on TSPO-PET-Measurable Immune Cell Activation in Multiple Sclerosis.
title: Watching cladribine's effect on immune activation show up on a PET scan
blurb: Uses TSPO-PET imaging to track immune cell activation in multiple sclerosis patients on oral cladribine, checking whether the drug's effect registers on the scan and not just in relapse counts.

original_title: Electrochemical Divergent Transformation of Flavonoids to Dihydroflavonols and 3-Iodoflavones
title: Same flavonoid, two different products, just flip the electrolyte
blurb: An electrochemical C–H functionalization turns flavonoids into either dihydroflavonols or 3-iodoflavones from the same starting material, the outcome set purely by which electrolyte and solvent you pick. Runs in an undivided cell at room temperature in air, no metal catalyst or added oxidant, and the mechanistic work actually pins down the intermediates instead of just claiming them.

original_title: Modulation of the TGF-β/Smad Signaling Pathway by a Bioactive Oxidized Polygonati Rhizoma Polysaccharide Crosslinked Chitosan Hydrogel as Therapeutic Carrier for Parkinson's Disease Treatment.
title: A polysaccharide-chitosan hydrogel aimed at Parkinson's, via TGF-β/Smad
blurb: An oxidized Polygonati Rhizoma polysaccharide crosslinked into a chitosan hydrogel, delivered as a therapeutic carrier for Parkinson's disease and working through modulation of the TGF-β/Smad signaling pathway.

original_title: Self‐Assembled Y 2 O 3 /Y(OH) 3 Heterojunction Nanosheets Hydrogel for Efficient Metal Resources Recovery
title: A hydrogel that doesn't fall apart while fishing out metal ions
blurb: Metal oxide hydrogels usually disintegrate in water because the metal ions hydrolyze too fast and the oxide-water interface won't hold. A two-step solvent-mediated self-assembly gets around that with a stable 3D Y2O3/Y(OH)3 nanosheet hydrogel built specifically for pulling metals out of solution.

original_title: Chemodivergent Synthesis of Indole Derivatives: [2 + 3]-Annulation of Oxindole-Derived MBH Carbonates with α-Enolic Dithioesters and Subsequent Branching Transformations
title: One annulation, several different indoles depending on which way you push it
blurb: Oxindole-derived MBH carbonates and α-enolic dithioesters run a [2+3] annulation that first lays down a thiophene scaffold still tethered to the oxindole, then branches into distinct indole derivatives depending on the follow-up step. Chemodivergence off one common intermediate rather than a separate route for each product.

original_title: Encapsulation of Inorganic NaX in Caged Sodium Alkoxide Clusters X@RONa: Scalable Syntheses, Structural Variations, and Mechanism Elucidation
title: Stuffing anions into sodium alkoxide cages, including the ones that don't want to leave
blurb: Just NaOR and ground NaX powder, heated in a nonpolar solvent, assembles dodecameric caged clusters encapsulating the X anion in high yield with little waste. The actual news is pushing the guest list past good leaving groups into borohydride, amide, and hydroxide, while the exterior alkyl groups get swapped around too. Atom-economical and apparently scalable, assuming the mechanism work they're pairing it with holds up.

original_title: Coordination‐Triggered Coupling‐Pathway Control in Organic Diradical Cations
title: A boron switch that decides how two radicals on a cation talk to each other
blurb: Diradicals are hard to tune because anything bolted onto them tends to react first. Here a boron center sits directly between two spin sources in an organic diradical cation, and coordinating something to that boron flips the antiferromagnetic coupling between them. A stimuli-responsive handle on a system that's usually all-or-nothing.

original_title: Reconfiguring Electrolyte Solvation Chemistry via In Situ Solvent Polymerization for High‐Performance Sodium‐Ion Batteries
title: Polymerizing the electrolyte solvent in place to fix sodium-ion battery's cathode problem
blurb: Ether electrolytes play nice with the anode but get chewed up at the cathode from poor oxidation resistance, and the usual fixes trade interface stability for bulk ion transport. This one polymerizes the solvent in situ into a liquid polymer electrolyte meant to hold both at once, fast ion transport and a stable interface, instead of picking one.

original_title: A Room-Temperature Synthesis of 3-Methylidene-2,3-dihydro-4-quinolones from o -Aniliopropargy Alcohols and Aldehydes
title: Quinolones at room temperature, no heat, just TfOH doing overtime
blurb: o-Anilinopropargyl alcohols plus aldehydes and 3 mol% TfOH, run at room temperature, give a set of 3-methylidene-2,3-dihydro-4-quinolones. The mechanism runs through acetalization with trimethyl orthoformate, a Meyer-Schuster rearrangement, a 1,3-migration, and conjugate addition before the methoxy group leaves, with that orthoformate reagent apparently pulling multiple jobs along the way. Low catalyst loading, broad substituent scope, good yields: this reads like a method people will actually reach for.

original_title: Programmable sequence-resolved in situ profiling of glycoRNA-protein interactomes by GlycoRNA-Map
title: Finally mapping what sticks to one specific glycoRNA instead of the whole pool
blurb: GlycoRNAs on the cell surface have only ever been studied as a pooled mess, so nobody knew the protein interactome of any single species. GlycoRNA-Map fixes that with a photocatalytic proximity-labeling setup where a sialic-acid-binding aptamer and an RNA-hybridization probe jointly lock onto one sequence-defined glycoRNA, then light-activated biotinylation tags whatever protein sits nearby. Sequence-resolved instead of averaged, which is the whole point.

original_title: Open Label Extension Study of Brentuximab Vedotin in Early dcSSc
title: Brentuximab vedotin's extension trial for early diffuse cutaneous scleroderma wraps up
blurb: A completed Phase 2 open-label extension testing brentuximab vedotin in early diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis, run out of London Health Sciences/Lawson. Just the trial closing out, no results posted yet.

original_title: Direct Evidence of a La–Te Bond and Bonding Regime Differences for Ln–C and Ln–Te in [K(18-Crown 6)(Cp″2LnTe3)] (Ln = La, Ce, and Nd)
title: Catching a lanthanum-tellurium bond in the act, and watching it differ from Ln-C
blurb: Nonclassical divalent lanthanide precursors reduce their way into [K(18-crown-6)(Cp''2LnTe3)] complexes for La, Ce, and Nd, giving direct evidence of an La-Te bond. DFT puts the frontier orbitals mostly on the [Te3]2- fragment, with the trivalent lanthanide mostly propping the tellurium chain up electronically rather than bonding it the way it would bond carbon. A look at how much of lanthanide-chalcogenide chemistry is real covalency versus an ion playing scaffold.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Directed Evolution of a Protein Catenane Reveals How Noncanonical Topology Modulates Sequence–Property Relationships
title: Tying a protein into a knot and then evolving it back to useful
blurb: Catenated dihydrofolate reductase, two mechanically interlocked rings folded into one compact domain, turns out broadly tolerant across different DHFR homologues, but soluble yield and catalytic activity still ride heavily on sequence. Directed evolution then claws back a lot of what the topology cost, giving a matched linear-versus-catenated comparison and a read on how much structural weirdness a protein can absorb before sequence stops bailing it out.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Advances in amidases and urethanases as depolymerization biocatalysts
title: Hunting enzymes that can actually chew through polyurethane
blurb: A review of amidases and urethanases that attack the amide and urethane bonds in polyamide and polyurethane plastics, helped along by bigger sequence databases and faster screening assays for finding and engineering them. Still a toolbox review, no single breakout enzyme to point at yet.

original_title: ANALYTICAL METHODS FOR SIMULTANEOUS ESTIMATION OF TELMISARTAN AND AMLODIPINE BESYLATE: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW
title: Yet another HPLC method review for a two-drug combo pill
blurb: A review rounding up the analytical methods, UV-vis, HPTLC, RP-HPLC and the rest, for measuring telmisartan and amlodipine besylate together in combination hypertension pills. Useful if you're validating a QC method, not if you want a new result.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Steering CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol, Hydrocarbons, and Higher Alcohols over In2O3-Based Catalysts
title: In2O3's defects are doing the chemistry, not the metal
blurb: A review on In2O3-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation, where oxygen-vacancy defect sites turn out to be what grabs and activates the CO2 and steers whether you end up with methanol, hydrocarbons or higher alcohols. It's a survey of how tuning those defects shifts selectivity, not a single new catalyst champion.

original_title: Dual-Modal Sensing of Enantiomeric Purity Using Chiral Au@Cu x S Nanoparticles
title: Gold-core nanoparticles that can tell your enantiomers apart two ways at once
blurb: Chiral Au@CuxS nanoparticles pair the gold core's plasmon resonance with the copper sulfide shell's semiconducting behavior, giving a dual readout, chiroptical plus NIR photothermal/photocatalytic response, for enantiomeric purity in one sensor. Handy if you want two independent confirmations instead of trusting one signal.

original_title: Dynamic Phosphate Hydrogen‐Bonded Networks Enable Biomedical‐Ready Stabilization of Black Phosphorus
title: The fix for black phosphorus falling apart in water is more phosphate
blurb: Black phosphorus normally oxidizes and falls apart fast in water, which kills its photothermal and drug-delivery promise. Letting it mildly oxidize in plain PBS buffer, the stuff already sitting on the shelf, builds a dynamic phosphate hydrogen-bonded network right at the surface that passivates it instead of destroying it.

original_title: Metal-Regulated Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer and Excimer Pathways to Achieve Full Spectrum Luminescence
title: One emitter, whole spectrum, just add zinc
blurb: A metal-organic emitter normally just does ESIPT, but Zn2+ coordination forces the molecules to stack, which opens up a second excimer emission channel on top. Switching between the enol, keto and excimer states covers blue through red, including white, off one scaffold.

original_title: Multiobjective VHH discovery through integrated high-throughput screening and AlphaFold3-guided structural prioritization
title: Picking better nanobodies by letting AlphaFold3 rank the hits
blurb: Pairs high-throughput screening with AlphaFold3-guided structural prioritization to pick VHH nanobodies against multiple objectives at once, folding a structure-prediction step into hit-picking instead of ranking on affinity alone.

original_title: Core-shell alginate-sulfonic acid networks crosslinked by multivalent cations (Ca(2+)/Al(3+)) for atmospheric water harvesting.
title: Alginate gel that drinks water straight out of the air
blurb: A core-shell alginate-sulfonic acid network crosslinked with a mix of Ca2+ and Al3+ ions, built for pulling water out of the atmosphere. A cheap biopolymer gel doing the job usually reserved for MOFs and desiccants.

original_title: Direct Synthesis of Cyclic Phosphoramides From White Phosphorus Prompted by Dichalcogenides
title: Skipping chlorine entirely to turn white phosphorus into phosphoramides
blurb: White phosphorus reacts straight with amino alcohols to give cyclic phosphoramides in one step, no chlorination needed, with organic disulfides or diphenyl diselenide doing double duty as mediator and reactant. Yields swing 34-95% depending on substrate, and the mechanism runs through a bicyclic phosphonium salt intermediate on the way to the P=O bond.

original_title: Photopolymerized antimicrobial hydrogels based on thiol-functionalized MXenes and in-situ generated silver nanoparticles.
title: MXene hydrogels that grow their own silver buckshot
blurb: A photopolymerized hydrogel built from thiol-functionalized MXenes that generates silver nanoparticles in situ, aimed at antimicrobial use. Light-cured and self-loading with silver rather than needing the particles pre-made and mixed in.

original_title: Benzofuran Synthesis from N -Aryloxysulfonamides and 2-Bromoallyl Sulfones via Sequential Treatment with Base and Acid
title: Benzofurans from a base-then-acid one-two punch, no metal in sight
blurb: Cesium carbonate first, then p-TsOH: that sequence turns N-aryloxysulfonamides and 2-bromoallyl sulfones into 2-(arylsulfonylmethyl)benzofurans. Base does a formal nucleophilic vinylic substitution, and the resulting O-aryl-N-vinyl hydroxylamine closes the ring itself via a room-temperature [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement. Swap in an allenoate ester and the same sequence hands you the benzofuran-ester version instead.

original_title: MIT used AI to develop new recipe for mRNA vaccines so they no longer need freezers and can sit at room temp for a full year or survive about 100F heat for two months which could finally let these vaccines reach poor countries without cold storage and even work as easy skin patches instead of shots.
title: MIT used AI to develop new recipe for mRNA vaccines so they no longer need freezers and can sit at room temp for a full year or survive about 100F heat for two months which could finally let these vaccines reach poor countries without cold storage and even work as easy skin patches instead of shots.

original_title: Antibody-drug conjugates in breast cancer: redefining targeted therapy
title: ADCs work, just not the way the magic bullet pitch says
blurb: A review arguing ADC efficacy in breast cancer isn't really about precision targeting. Extracellular payload release, bystander killing, off-tumor uptake, and immune effects all pitch in, so the clean 'selective delivery' story is mostly marketing.

original_title: Development of a Polypeptide-Based Platform to Construct Antibody-Drug Conjugates with High Potency.
title: A polypeptide scaffold for building more potent ADCs
blurb: A platform that swaps the usual linker chemistry for a polypeptide-based carrier, pitched as yielding higher-potency ADCs. No numbers to chew on yet, just the design.

original_title: Regulatory Considerations in Supplemental BLA Submission for the Addition of Drug-Linker Manufacturing Sites in Antibody-Drug Conjugates
title: Adding a second ADC factory means refiling with the FDA
blurb: Walks through why bringing a new drug-linker manufacturing site online for an already-approved ADC triggers a Supplemental BLA, usually as a Prior Approval Supplement. Makes sense once you remember the linker chemistry is directly tied to stability and safety. More paperwork than science, but the kind that decides how fast capacity actually scales.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Proximity‐Induced Disulfide Rebridging Enables Modular Construction of Stable Antibody–Drug Conjugates
title: A disulfide rebridging reagent that doesn't make you pick speed or stability
blurb: Existing disulfide rebridging chemistry forces a tradeoff: fast conjugation with shaky stability, or a stable linkage that reacts too slowly. These heterotrifunctional fluoropyridine reagents are kinetically differentiated enough to get both, so native antibodies get site-specific, stable ADCs without the usual compromise.

original_title: NorthStar secures up to $185 million to scale Actinium-225 production - The Pharma Letter
title: NorthStar gets $185M to make more Actinium-225
blurb: Funding aimed squarely at scaling Ac-225 production, the alpha-emitter that's been the supply bottleneck for all the targeted alpha therapy trials people keep designing around it. Money doesn't equal yield yet, but it's pointed at the right problem.

original_title: Metabolic Engineering and Bioprocess Optimization Strategies Promote l -Azidohomoalanine Biosynthesis in Fed-Batch Bioreactor Culture
title: Making the click-chemistry amino acid without the eye-watering price tag
blurb: Azidohomoalanine subs for methionine in translation and is the handle most bioorthogonal click labeling runs through, but it's been too pricey for scale-up. This takes a cheap-azide biosynthesis route and actually runs it in a fed-batch bioreactor, aiming to make labeled recombinant protein production routine instead of a boutique trick.

original_title: From Dual Targeting to Clinical Validation: A Translational Framework for Bispecific Antibody–Drug Conjugates
title: Bispecific ADCs have to earn their extra complexity, this review sets the bar
blurb: A systematic review of bispecific antibody-drug conjugates, designed to fix the heterogeneous antigen expression and poor tumor-versus-normal discrimination that trip up conventional ADCs. The point isn't cataloguing preclinical dual-antigen designs, it's spelling out what clinical evidence would actually justify the added engineering over a plain ADC.

original_title: Multi-parameter optimization of a novel anti-TROP2 MMAE antibody-drug-conjugate for solid tumor therapy
title: A second shot at an anti-TROP2 MMAE ADC, after the first one got stopped by toxicity
blurb: TROP2 is already a validated ADC target via sacituzumab govitecan and datopotamab deruxtecan, but an earlier anti-TROP2 auristatin ADC, PF-06664178, couldn't be dosed effectively because of skin rash, mucosal inflammation, and neutropenia. TroptimAb-SL-MMAE is a multi-parameter-optimized redesign for solid tumors, presumably built to dodge that same wall.

original_title: Brain Landscape In Situ Crosslinking Mass Spectrometry (BLIS-XL-MS) Enables Global Analysis of Protein Structural Remodeling in the Brain.
title: Crosslinking mass spec, now mapped across the whole brain
blurb: A new in situ crosslinking MS method for tracking protein structural remodeling across brain tissue rather than one protein at a time. Still a preprint, so no independent replication yet, but the pitch is going from single-protein snapshots to a brain-wide map.

original_title: Telix To Acquire Radioisotope Supplier ITM For Up To $2.35 Billion To Build Radiopharmaceutical Powerhouse - Pulse 2.0
title: Telix buys its way to a radioisotope supply chain, $2.35B for ITM
blurb: Telix is acquiring radioisotope supplier ITM for up to $2.35 billion, betting that owning the isotope pipeline matters more than owning any one drug as radiopharmaceuticals get crowded. A supply-chain play wearing an acquisition headline.

original_title: Quality by Design (QbD)-Based Green RP-HPLC Method Development and Validation for Concurrent Estimation of Atenolol and Amlodipine in Combined Tablet Formulations.
title: A greener, by-the-numbers HPLC method for two blood pressure drugs
blurb: QbD tuning applied to a reverse-phase HPLC method that measures atenolol and amlodipine together in the same tablet, built around cutting the solvent and the usual nasty reagents older methods ran on. Another combo-pill assay validated, this time with the green chemistry box checked.
venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical Research and Applications

original_title: First-in-human dosimetry and biodistribution of [89Zr]Zr-oxine-labeled autologous leukocytes using PET/CT
title: PET-tracking your own white blood cells, Zr-89 style
blurb: Four healthy women had their own leukocytes labeled with Zr-89-oxine and got PET/CT scans out to 72 hours, just to nail down radiation dose and confirm nothing bad happens. No disease imaging yet, this is the safety and dosimetry groundwork for later tracking infection, inflammation, or cell therapies.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Enantio- and Regioselective Ni-Catalyzed Hydroarylation of Alkenes and Alkynes to Form C–N Axially Chiral Heterobiaryls
title: Nickel catalysis builds axially chiral C-N biaryls straight from alkenes
blurb: An Ni/NHC-catalyzed hydroarylation adds unactivated alkenes directly across the C-N axis, skipping a separate coupling step and getting both regio- and enantiocontrol in one go. Reported scope is broad with good to excellent selectivity, and atom economy is the actual selling point.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Sensitizing tumor response to topoisomerase I antibody-drug conjugate by selective CDK7 inhibition.
title: Priming topoisomerase-I ADCs with a CDK7 hit
blurb: CDK7 inhibition used to make tumors more responsive to a topoisomerase I-targeted antibody-drug conjugate. Thin on detail, but the logic is straightforward: knock down a resistance pathway first, then let the ADC do its job.

original_title: Silk Fibroin Nanofiber–Immobilized Horseradish Peroxidase Enables Continuous Preparation of Injectable Hydrogels With Negligible Residual Enzyme for Drug Delivery
title: An enzyme reactor that builds hydrogels without leaving the enzyme behind
blurb: HRP pinned onto ground silk fibroin nanofibers in a flow-through reactor, so it keeps crosslinking hyaluronic acid into injectable hydrogels continuously without free enzyme ending up in the product. Residual HRP is the usual immunogenicity worry with peroxidase-cured gels, so making it negligible is the point.

original_title: ANTIBODY-DRUG CONJUGATES IN BREAST CANCER: BENCH TO BEDSIDE INSIGHTS ON MECHANISM, EFFICACY, AND SAFETY
title: ADCs in breast cancer, the bench-to-bedside recap
blurb: A literature review walking through how antibody-drug conjugates work, how well they perform, and how safe they are in breast cancer, with HER2 and TROP-2 as the targets getting the attention. Nothing new generated here, just a synthesis of what's already out there.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Native Mass Spectrometry Reveals Distinct Effects of Linker Length and Targeting-Ligand Identity on PROTAC Ternary Complexes
title: Native mass spec maps how PROTAC linkers shape the ternary complex
blurb: Ion mobility, surface-induced dissociation, and variable-temperature ESI combined to show that both linker length and which targeting ligand you pick reshape the PROTAC-target-E3 ligase complex's structure and interfaces. That conformational landscape is exactly what's hard to pin down by other means, so the method is as much the headline as the finding.

original_title: Systematic PEGylation optimization of Dar3A-based FAP-targeted PET probes and first-in-human study.
title: Dialing in the PEG on a FAP-targeted PET probe, then testing it in people
blurb: Systematic PEGylation tuning of the Dar3A FAP-targeting PET probe, carried through to a first-in-human study. Little detail beyond that, but going straight from linker optimization to human imaging is the notable part.

original_title: ANTIBODY-DRUG CONJUGATES IN BREAST CANCER: BENCH TO BEDSIDE INSIGHTS ON MECHANISM, EFFICACY, AND SAFETY
title: Another HER2/TROP-2 ADC review for breast cancer
blurb: Same ground as most of these reviews: mechanism, linker-payload-antibody breakdown, and the efficacy and safety data for HER2- and TROP-2-directed ADCs in breast cancer, compiled rather than new. Useful as a reference, not a result.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: Cross-Species Profiling of Itaconate-Mediated Modifications by a Universal Probe
title: One probe to catch itaconate modifications in both man and microbe
blurb: isoC3A profiles both cysteine itaconation and lysine itaconylation in the same shot, across eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells, where earlier bioorthogonal probes were biased toward one modification or one kingdom. They ran it on Salmonella-infected macrophages and caught the modifications as they happened, which the older biased probes couldn't do at all.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Radical Hydrofunctionalization Using Light Driven, Reductive Cobalt Hydride Catalysis
title: Light-driven cobalt hydrides doing MHAT's usual tricks
blurb: A conspectus-style rundown of using photochemistry to make cobalt hydrides for metal-hydride HAT catalysis. The weak Co-H bond makes H-atom addition to an olefin thermodynamically downhill, which is where MHAT gets its sharp regiochemistry, and the resulting carbon radical then gets steered into a range of hydrofunctionalization products. Reads like a tour of a research program rather than one new reaction.

original_title: Atroposelective Desymmetrizing Iodination via Chiral Phosphoric Acid Catalysis: Synthesis of Axially Chiral Biaryl Phosphine Oxides
title: An iodine atom to lock in axial chirality, no handles required
blurb: A chiral phosphoric acid catalyzes desymmetrizing iodination of phosphine oxides that have nothing to hydrogen-bond to, going through noncovalent contacts between catalyst, substrate, and the iodinating reagent instead. Excellent yields and ee across di-tert-butyl and dicyclohexyl variants, with no pre-functionalization or additives needed, which is the actual selling point here.

original_title: Discovery and Total Synthesis of Seco -acorane Sesquiterpenoids from Chloranthus holostegius : Determination of Absolute Configuration and Spontaneous Acetalization
title: A sesquiterpenoid that acetalizes itself before you can pin its stereochemistry
blurb: New seco/nor-acorane sesquiterpenoids from Chloranthus holostegius, including an aldehyde-bearing one that spontaneously forms an acetal with whatever methanol (even CD3OD) happens to be around. The flexible side chain's absolute configuration wasn't settled by isolation alone, so they ran a redox-relay Heck total synthesis and made the natural products plus their methanol and methanol-d4 acetal adducts to prove it out.

original_title: Telescoped Two-Step Continuous-Flow Synthesis of Nevirapine Enabled by the On-Demand Generation of NaHMDS
title: Nevirapine made in flow, generating its own base on the way through
blurb: A fully continuous, telescoped two-step flow synthesis of the HIV drug nevirapine that makes NaHMDS on demand and uses it for both stages, skipping isolation of the cyclization intermediate entirely. Ten minutes total residence time, which is the kind of process paper that only works if someone's willing to handle NaHMDS continuously rather than in a flask.

original_title: Catalytic Desymmetrizing Carbonyl–Amine Condensation Reaction to Construct Axially Chiral Diaryl Ethers
title: Chiral diaryl ethers via condensation, not the usual coupling route
blurb: A desymmetrizing carbonyl-amine condensation between prochiral diamino diaryl ethers and cyclobutane-1,3-diones hits up to 99% ee, the first time anyone's run prochiral aromatic amines through this kind of asymmetric condensation. The cyclobutanediones noticeably beat other carbonyl partners on both reactivity and selectivity, so that's the variant actually doing the work.

original_title: Copper(I)‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogermylation of 3,3‐Disubstituted Cyclopropenes
title: An asymmetric entry point into organogermanium chemistry
blurb: CuOAc alone catalyzes asymmetric hydrogermylation of disubstituted cyclopropenes, giving chiral organogermanes with high dr and ee in a space that's barely been touched catalytically. Swap to Cu(CH3CN)4PF6 plus an added base and the reaction just dies, so the copper carboxylate itself is doing something specific here, not acting as a generic Lewis acid stand-in.

original_title: Monofluoromethylphenylalanine: A Sensitive 19F Probe for Protein Conformational Dynamics In Vitro and in Cells
title: A better 19F tag for watching proteins move, cells included
blurb: A new 19F-labeled unnatural amino acid, CH2F-phenylalanine, aimed at the standard complaint with 19F NMR probes: cramped chemical shift dispersion and poor sensitivity to conformational change, which gets worse once you leave buffer for an actual cell. Claimed to read out protein dynamics better both in vitro and in cells.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Radical, Not Ionic: The Mechanochemical Zincke Nitration of Phenols
title: The Zincke nitration's mechanism finally gets pinned down, and it's radical
blurb: Ball-milling NaNO2 and NaHSO4 generates nitrous acid in situ and nitrates phenols, reproducing the halogen-displacement chemistry the classical Zincke nitration is known for, including ipso nitration of halophenols. That reactivity has always been assumed to run through an ionic pathway; this mechanochemical version says it's radical instead.

original_title: Regio- and Diastereo-Controlled (5 + 2) Cycloaddition of gem -Difluorocyclopropenes and Oxidopyridinium Ions
title: A one-pot route into difluorinated azatricyclic cages
blurb: A (5+2) cycloaddition between gem-difluorocyclopropenes and oxidopyridinium ions builds the 3,3-difluoro-9-azatricyclo[3.3.1.02,4]nonane core directly, exclusively exo, with moderate to good yields across a broad substrate range. They back it up with a gram-scale run and further derivatization, so this reads like an actual usable method rather than just a scope table.

original_title: Extracting Latent Sequence-Function Information from Directed Evolution to Design Improved C-H Azidases
title: The directed evolution data everyone throws away was apparently useful
blurb: Standard directed evolution sequences only the top hits and discards the sequence-function information sitting in the rest of the library. This bins screened variants by activity level, pools each bin, and long-read sequences them to recover that latent signal, using it to design improved C-H azidases. Same screening effort, more information squeezed out of it.

original_title: 3D Printable and Electrically Conductive Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogel for Cardiac and Vascular Tissue Engineering Applications.
title: A hydrogel that's both 3D printable and electrically conductive
blurb: A hyaluronic acid hydrogel engineered to be both electrically conductive and printable in 3D, aimed at cardiac and vascular tissue scaffolds. Not much else to go on here, but for tissue that has to carry an electrical signal, a conductive printable gel is exactly the right ask.

original_title: Total Synthesis of Antrimycins A and D
title: First total synthesis of the anti-TB antrimycins
blurb: Antrimycins A and D are Streptomyces heptapeptides pulled from an anti-tuberculosis screen, built from four non-proteinogenic amino acids including a dehydropiperazic acid and an E-dehydroisoleucine. They've been eyed as leads for new TB drugs since discovery, but apparently nobody had actually made them from scratch until this paper.

original_title: 口腔鳞癌近红外光免疫治疗：机制与临床转化
title: NIR photoimmunotherapy for oral cancer, reviewed from mechanism to clinic
blurb: A review of near-infrared photoimmunotherapy for oral squamous cell carcinoma: antibody-photoabsorber conjugates plus 690 nm light trigger immunogenic cell death, so it kills locally and stirs up the immune system at once. Real-world data so far backs its safety and efficacy at oral sites, but patient selection and how deep the light actually reaches remain the sticking points, and the authors flag that current efficacy predictors are thin, with CD39+CD8+ T cells the most promising lead. They're calling for multicenter RCTs before anyone gets ahead of the evidence.

original_title: Absorbing-molecule-induced optical clearing enhances Cerenkov luminescence imaging of radiopharmaceutical distribution.
title: Clearing tissue optically to sharpen Cerenkov imaging
blurb: Uses absorbing molecules to optically clear tissue, which sharpens Cerenkov luminescence imaging of where a radiopharmaceutical actually distributes. An imaging-method paper with no numbers given, so the real test is how much resolution it buys you.

original_title: Bulk Post-Polymerization Modification of a Single-Crystalline 2D Polymer via the Katritzky Reaction: A Modular Platform for Functional 2D Materials
title: Modifying a 2D polymer after it's already made
blurb: Topochemical 2D polymers are already a pain, you need monomers preorganized in a crystal lattice with their reactive groups close enough to actually link up, and modifying them afterward (routine for 1D polymers) is rarer still. Existing pyrylium-based 2DPs choke on steric clashes from their di-tert-butyl groups; this gets around that with the Katritzky reaction, opening the door to functionalizing these materials after the fact instead of only during synthesis.

original_title: C–H Activations with a T-Shaped 14 Electron PNP-Rhodium(I) Complex: Step-by-Step Formation and Reactivity of (Vinylidene)rhodium Complexes
title: Watching a Rh pincer complex turn an alkyne into a vinylidene, step by step
blurb: A T-shaped 14-electron PNP-rhodium(I) complex with a carbazole backbone reacts with terminal alkynes to form an isolable alkynyl(hydrido)Rh(III) intermediate first, then converts intramolecularly into the vinylidene. The nice part is they could actually isolate and characterize each step instead of just inferring the mechanism.

original_title: Electrochemical Hydroformylation with a Homogeneous Rhodium Catalyst
title: Hydroformylation that runs on electrons instead of hydrogen gas
blurb: Electrochemical hydroformylation swaps H2 from steam methane reforming for electrons off the grid, and this version uses a homogeneous Rh catalyst instead of the usual heterogeneous ones. The numbers are modest, though: 1.1 mA/cm2 partial current density and 29% Faradaic efficiency, so this reads as proof of concept rather than something ready to compete on rate.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Stereoselective Glycosylation of Amides with Glycal Catalyzed by a Solid–Liquid Phase-Transfer and Proton-Transfer Dual-Functional Pyridinium Catalyst
title: One catalyst, two jobs, for glycosylating amides with glycals
blurb: 2-Pentafluorophenylpyridinium tetrafluoroborate handles both the phase-transfer and proton-transfer steps needed for stereoselective glycosylation of amides with glycals, and it covers glucals, previously untouched 6-deoxy sugars like rhamnals, xylals, and arabinals, and even complex bioactive peptides. 2-Deoxyglycosylamides have been annoying to make cleanly, so one catalyst spanning that much substrate range is the actual news.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Strategic Formation of Indoles Using Phenyl Hydrazine as a Key Reagent
title: A field guide to building indoles from phenylhydrazine
blurb: A review tying classical Fischer indolization to the newer Rh(III)/Ru(II)/Co(III)-catalyzed C–H activation routes, hydroformylation-assisted variants, and acid-promoted condensations, all starting from phenylhydrazine. Handy as a map of the state of the art, though it's a survey, not a new reaction.

original_title: Widespread Biosynthesis of Thiohistidine Dipeptides in Bacteria
title: Ergothioneine has a lot more relatives hiding in bacterial genomes
blurb: Thio/seleno-imidazoles like ergothioneine get their C–S or C–Se bonds from nonheme iron sulfoxide and selenoxide synthases, and the authors used those enzymes as a bioinformatic hook to go hunting for related biosynthesis across bacteria. Thiohistidine dipeptide production turns out to be widespread rather than a quirk of a few species, which suggests the known TSI chemical space is still an undercount.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of ( E,E,Z )-Humulene-Derived Natural Products
title: Making humulene's overlooked Z-isomer cousins
blurb: Nearly everything known about humulene-derived meroterpenoids comes from the easy (E,E,E) isomer. This paper builds the (E,E,Z) line instead, opening with a selective oxidative double-bond isomerization to make (10S)-hydroxyhumulene, then using that as the entry point into natural products nobody has made before. First synthesis of its kind, so the biology is still an open question.

original_title: Transneuronal Transport of Ligand-Conjugated Upconversion Nanoparticles from the Peripheral to the Central Nervous System.
title: Nanoparticles hitching a ride from nerves into the brain
blurb: Ligand-conjugated upconversion nanoparticles apparently travel transneuronally from the peripheral nervous system into the CNS. That's the whole claim as far as the title goes, but a nanoparticle route past the blood-brain barrier via nerve transport would be worth a closer look if it pans out.

original_title: Visible Light-Enabled Oxo-Alkylation of Styrenes with Aliphatic Alcohol Derivatives for the Synthesis of α-Alkyl Ketones
title: Alkyl radicals that break the scaffold instead of just stripping the oxygen
blurb: N-alkoxyphthalimides under visible light generate alkoxy radicals that fragment rather than deoxygenate, so instead of patching an alcohol back together you get a fresh alkyl radical that adds onto styrenes to build alpha-alkyl ketones. Works across primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols and tolerates late-stage modification, which deconstructive methods aren't usually known for.

original_title: Redox-Active Bipyridine–Iron Half-Sandwich Complexes for Catalytic Carbene Transfer
title: A bipyridine-iron half-sandwich finally gets its turn at carbene transfer
blurb: Bpy ligands are everywhere in transition-metal catalysis except, until now, on half-sandwich iron. The new (η5-C5Me5)Fe(bpy)(X) family gives a low-valent 17-electron species on single-electron reduction, and that open-shell character is what drives the catalytic carbene transfer rather than anything unusual at the metal.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Diagnostic performance of multiparametric model integrating ¹⁸F-MFBG PET/CT imaging parameters and clinical factors for differentiating neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma: a preliminary study
title: Telling neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma off a PET scan
blurb: A multiparametric model pairs 18F-MFBG PET/CT features with clinical factors to try to separate these two tumor types without a biopsy. It's flagged as a preliminary study, so treat it as proof of concept rather than a diagnostic swap just yet.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Dehydrogenation of Biomass‐Derived Aromatic Diol to Value‐Added Acyloin and Hydrogen Production Over Zn 0.3 Cd 0.7 S Solid Solution With Defect Clusters and Its Photocatalytic Mechanism
title: Defect-engineered ZnCdS splits the dehydrogenation job from the hydrogen job
blurb: Acceptorless photocatalytic dehydrogenation usually stalls because oxidation and proton reduction compete for the same charge carriers. Here Mo-substitution/Zn-vacancy defect clusters built into Zn0.3Cd0.7S physically separate those two jobs, converting a biomass aromatic diol to acyloin while producing hydrogen on the side. The defect-cluster design is the actual contribution, not just another photocatalyst recipe.

original_title: Design Changes That Lead to Large Effects in Photocatalysis: A Ruthenium–Terpyridine Complex Stable and Active Enough to Outperform [Ru(bpy)3]2+
title: A ruthenium-terpyridine dye built to finally beat Ru(bpy)3
blurb: A new heteroleptic Ru-terpyridine complex is both more stable and about an order of magnitude more active for hydrogen evolution than the usual reference, thanks to a push-pull ligand design. Under blue light it holds a TON above 3500 and keeps pumping out H2 for six days straight, more than double what Ru(bpy)3²⁺ manages under the same conditions. Terpyridine sensitizers normally die fast, so the stability here is as much the story as the TON.

original_title: Solvent‐Free Synthesis of Covalent Organic Frameworks: Achievements and Challenges
title: Making COFs without the solvent bath
blurb: A review rounding up solvent-free routes to covalent organic frameworks: mechanochemical grinding, ionothermal melts, flux-assisted polymerization, vapor-assisted interfaces. Framed around what each buys you over the usual solvothermal cook and where each still comes up short, so don't expect one method to win outright.

original_title: Ultramild conversion of nitrobenzene to aniline mediated by metal organic alloy NiGraf in green solvent
title: Reducing nitrobenzene to aniline at 35°C with a recyclable nickel-graphene alloy
blurb: NiGraf, nickel entrapped in reduced graphene oxide, pushes nitrobenzene to aniline with hydrazine at just 35°C and ambient pressure in a water/THF mix. The selling point is mild conditions plus a catalyst you can recover and reuse, for a reduction that normally wants heat or pressure to get there.

original_title: NovAccel Expands U.S. Presence to Advance Global Actinium-225 Supply - GlobeNewswire
title: Another company chasing the Ac-225 bottleneck
blurb: NovAccel is expanding its US presence to scale up actinium-225 production. Standard capacity-expansion news, the kind every Ac-225 story turns into until someone actually ships enough isotope to unstick the alpha-therapy trials waiting on it.

original_title: Converting Nonspecific Adsorption into Bioaffinity Recognition: Defect-Engineered MOF-808 Creates a Synergistic Enzyme Interface for Selective Ligand Fishing and Closed-Loop Target Confirmation
title: Defect-engineering a MOF so it binds like an enzyme, not flypaper
blurb: Mild NaOH etching turns MOF-808 into a hierarchically porous scaffold with exposed Zr4+ sites that immobilize neuraminidase while keeping its native fold intact, checked by CD spectroscopy. The result is an enzyme-MOF interface that fishes out ligands by actual bioaffinity instead of the usual indiscriminate sticking.

original_title: Tandem Catalysis Sites in Co‐NO/C for Efficient and Scalable Electrocatalytic Nitrate to Ammonia Conversion
title: Two cobalt sites splitting the nitrate-to-ammonia job
blurb: A Co3O4/Co4N tandem catalyst embedded in conductive carbon, where Co3O4 handles nitrate adsorption and activation and Co4N next door supplies the active hydrogen for reduction. Dividing the labor is the point, since getting both steps going at once is usually what trips this reaction up.

original_title: [64/67Cu]-FAP theranostics in combination with immunotherapy in a preclinical model of TNBC.
title: Pairing FAP-targeted copper theranostics with immunotherapy in TNBC mice
blurb: Cu-64 for imaging and Cu-67 for therapy, both on the same FAP-targeting ligand, tested together with immunotherapy in a preclinical triple-negative breast cancer model. It's a Research Square preprint, so mouse data only for now.

original_title: Abundance is not survival: Intratumoural immune-cell fate as a missing endpoint in antibody-drug conjugate and checkpoint blockade combinations for triple-negative breast cancer
title: Counting immune cells in the tumor isn't the same as knowing what happens to them
blurb: A review arguing that ADC plus checkpoint blockade trials in TNBC keep tracking how many immune cells show up intratumourally, when survival and function of those cells once there is the endpoint that's actually missing. Obvious once stated, and apparently nobody's measuring it.

original_title: From Direct to Alternating Current Electrosynthesis: Transition-Metal-Catalyzed Oxidative Cross-Coupling with Hydrogen Evolution
title: Switching electrosynthesis from direct to alternating current to fix the catalyst mismatch
blurb: A conspectus on transition-metal-catalyzed oxidative cross-coupling with hydrogen evolution, built around the long-standing mismatch between electron transfer at the electrode and how fast the catalyst actually turns over in solution. The pitch is that driving the reaction with AC instead of DC gets around it. It's a review of the authors' own program, so judge the framing accordingly.

original_title: Copper(I)‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogermylation of 3,3‐Disubstituted Cyclopropenes
title: Finally a decent route to chiral organogermanes
blurb: CuOAc-catalyzed hydrogermylation of 3,3-disubstituted cyclopropenes gives chiral organogermanium compounds in high dr and ee, a compound class that's been oddly neglected. Swap in Cu(CH3CN)4PF6 plus a base instead and the reaction just dies, so the copper carboxylate itself is doing real mechanistic work, not just sitting there as a counterion.

original_title: Synthesis of α‐ C ‐Glycoside Conjugates Promoted by 4CzIPN‐Based Porous Organic Polymers Through Giese‐Like Reaction of Glycosyl Bromides in Batch and Continuous Flow
title: A reusable photocatalyst for building C-glycosides, in batch or flow
blurb: Glycosyl bromides generate anomeric radicals under visible light that add Giese-style to electron-poor olefins to form the C-glycosidic bond under mild conditions. After confirming 4CzIPN itself works, they heterogenized it into a porous polymer so the catalyst can be reused and run continuously instead of refilled flask by flask.

original_title: Direct Asymmetric Synthesis of Chiral β‐Hydroxy‐α‐Amino Amides via PLP ‐Inspired Biomimetic Aldol Reaction
title: Skipping the racemization-prone route to β-hydroxy-α-amino amides
blurb: A pyridoxal catalyst standing in for PLP runs a direct aldol on glycinamides, building chiral β-hydroxy-α-amino amides in one step instead of making the amino acid first and amidating afterward, which is where the stereocenter usually gets scrambled. Glycinamides are sluggish and the aldol products unstable, so getting this to go directly is the actual trick.

original_title: Iterative Multimutant Design Creates a Family-Like Enzyme Ensemble
title: Breeding an enzyme family instead of evolving one enzyme at a time
blurb: Starting from human NNMT's weak, incidental azole N-methylation activity, they iteratively designed and screened combinations of energetically compatible mutations, screening only 1,600 clones over three rounds. What came out is a spread of related variants rather than one optimized specialist, which is the actual point: natural enzyme families get their breadth by diversifying a scaffold, something one-substrate-at-a-time directed evolution normally can't reproduce.

original_title: Copper‐Mediated C─H Amination of Hetero (Arene) Scaffolds via Amide Directing Group: Unlocking Bioactive Pharmacophore for Next‐Generation Drug Discovery
title: Copper picks up C-H amination where palladium used to dominate
blurb: An amide directing group lets copper run C-H amination on (hetero)arene scaffolds to build nitrogen-containing pharmacophores, pitched as a cheaper, less toxic stand-in for the usual precious-metal chemistry. No scope or yields in view yet, so this reads as a positioning paper more than a finished method.
